 I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No. 229 of 2012
Common Judgment

:
(as per Hon'ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman) The lis involved in both the appeals and the parties are one and the same, both the appeals were heard together and decided by way of this common judgment.
The parties as arrayed in F.C.A.No.297 of 2012 are referred herein for convenience.

2. Heard Sri Rupendra Mahendera, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant-husband in F.C.A. No. 297 of 2012 and respondent in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 and Sri Kiran Palakurthy, learned counsel representing Smt. Srilatha Palakurthy, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent-wife in F.C.A.No.297 of 2012 and appellant in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012.
Perused the record.

3. Appellant-husband filed F.C.O.P.No.183 of 2009 against the respondent-wife, under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, seeking dissolution of marriage performed on KL,J &
PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 24.06.1999 on the ground of cruelty and desertion.

Vide order, dated 04.06.2012, the learned Judge, Family Court,
Ranga Reddy District, allowed O.P.No.183 of 2009 filed by the appellant- husband by dissolving the marriage of appellant and respondent performed on 24.06.1999.
The learned Judge also directed the appellant-husband to pay maintenance of Rs.5,00,000/- to the respondent-wife and his son towards permanent alimony within two months from the date of the order.

4. Feeling aggrieved by the said order of granting divorce, wife preferred an appeal vide F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 and this Court vide order dated 09.08.2012 restrained appellant-husband from contracting remarriage till further orders.
Likewise, feeling aggrieved by the said order of granting an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- towards permanent alimony, husband preferred F.C.A.No.297 of 2012.

5. CONTENTIONS OF THE APPELLANT-HUSBAND:
a) His marriage with the respondent was performed on 24.06.1999 as per Hindu rites and customs and it is an arranged marriage.

sentences.text: KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 b) The said marriage was consummated.
They were blessed with a son on 23.09.2000 by name Abi Ram Reddy.
c) At the time of marriage, respondent studied only upto intermediate, he encouraged her to continue her studies.
Therefore, with his encouragement, respondent completed her B.Com and M.B.A by September 2006 through distance education system.

d) He has purchased a TVS Scooty in the month of April, 2004 and plot bearing No.53 admeasuring 300 sq.yards forming part of Sy.No.261 to 266 and 290 at Nizampet Village, Quthbullapur Mandal,
Ranga Reddy District for the benefit of his family in the name of respondent through registered sale deed bearing document No.8106 of 2002 dated 27.09.2002.
e) On the advice of respondent, he gave an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to her brother i.e., Mr. Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy in the month of November 2004 for the purpose of constructing a room, compound wall and digging a bore well in the said plot.
The said Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy did not complete the same and he has not returned the said money.
KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 f)
The brother of respondent has started giving imaginary and illusive advises to the respondent and he has succeeded in the same.
At his instance, respondent started behaving adamantly with the appellant.
She also got support of her maternal aunt Smt. Prabhavathi.
g) On the advice of respondent, appellant has shifted his family to R.N. Reddy Nagar in the last week of February, 2004.
h) Appellant joined his son in Dilsukhnagar Public School, Karmanghat Branch.
i) Her maternal aunt Smt. Prabhavathi, used to run a boys hostel for Engineering students.
Appellant used to visit the said hostel on holidays.

During his visits, he observed change of attitude of the respondent and she was actively participating in the day-to-day business of the said hostel.
j) She never cared to lookafter the minimum necessities of the appellant and his son and also the matrimonial relation.
k) The said Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy used to visit the respondent frequently.

At his instance,
respondent harassed him both physically and mentally.
KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 l)
On 08.07.2006, appellant came to know from Smt. Prabhavathi that respondent left the house and was residing at Kukatpally with her parents.

sentences.text: Her father was working as Driver in APSRTC.
n) Appellant went to the house of respondent's parents on the same day, but they did not allow him to enter into the house.
They have insulted and humiliated him.
o) He had also conducted mediations through well wishers and there was no use.
p) He has personally visited the house of parents of respondent with his father on 21.10.2006.
They have abused them in filthy and unparliamentarily language.
q) Finally, they have informed the appellant that respondent is no more interested to continue the matrimonial relationship with him on the ground that he is having 'night blindness'.
He could not lose hope in continuing matrimonial relationship with respondent.
r) Thereafter, he made several efforts through well-wishers and elders.
KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 s)

When he tried to visit the house of parents of respondent on 15.04.2007, her parents along with mediators, brother Mr.Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy and sons of Smt.Prabhavathi closed the outer doors and assaulted the appellant and his father on the instigation of the respondent and her mother.
t) They have also caused injuries to the appellant.
With great difficulty, u) with the assistance of his father and mediators, he could come out from the clutches of the respondent and her men.

Appellant did not make any complaint to the Police though he suffered physical and mental injuries,
with a hope that respondent may realize her mistake and join his company.
v) He also wrote a letter on 17.04.2008 mentioning all the aforestated facts and requested the respondent to join his company.
There was no use.

6. On the other hand, respondent entered into an Agreement- cum-G.P.A. for development of the aforesaid plot purchased by the appellant in the name of respondent at the instance of her brother,
without even informing to the appellant.
As per the said agreement, 30% of the developed area falls to the share of KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 respondent and 70% to the builder.
Therefore, appellant has filed a suit vide O.S.No.512 of 2008 seeking cancellation of the Sale Deed and also cancellation of Agreement-cum-G.P.A. dated 18.04.2007.

He also filed an interlocutory application vide I.A.No.105 of 2008 restraining the builder from changing the nature of the property which was dismissed by the learned II Additional District Judge, R.R. District.

sentences.text: 7. The appellant used to work as Cane Regulative Inspector under the Government of Andhra Pradesh and he is residing at various places at Nizambad District.
Thereafter, due to adamant attitude of the respondent, appellant lost hope of restitution of conjugal right.
Therefore, he has filed the aforesaid OP seeking dissolution of marriage.

sentences.text: Respondent filed counter denying the said allegations.
According to her, the aforesaid plot was purchased by her father by selling out her property at Housing Board, Kukatpally.
a) On the demand of appellant, her father paid an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- to him by way of DD.
In fact, the appellant has to pay an amount of Rs.80,000/- to her father.

KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 b) The appellant is having defective vision which was not disclosed to her at the time of marriage.
When it has come to the notice of the respondent, she and her parents taken the appellant to various hospitals for examination and treatment including L.V.Prasad Eye Hospital.
c) On seeing appellant's condition, the parents of respondent were taking more care about the welfare of the respondent and her son.
d) In fact, the behavior of appellant was indifferent and respondent could not understand the problem of the appellant, but since 2005 his behavior became intolerable and he used to suspect everyone.
Appellant was taken to Asha Hospital, Banjara Hills, where it was informed that due to eye problem and poor vision, he has become psychic and advised to take counseling.
e) Appellant continued his matrimonial life and refused to take treatment.
Due to unbearable harassment of the appellant, respondent tried to commit suicide on 26.02.2008.
f) Appellant did not come to Hyderabad despite receipt of the aforesaid information.
KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 g)
Respondent was admitted in Mamata Hospital as inpatient till 03.03.2008.
However, vide his letter dated 17.04.2008, he has requested the respondent to join his company by making certain unwanted allegations.
Thus, according to the respondent, she never subjected the appellant to cruelty as alleged by him.
9. To prove the said allegation of cruelty and desertion, appellant-husband examined himself as PW.1, his father as PW.2, independent witness/relatives/mediators as PW.3 and PW.4.
He has filed Exs.P1 to P14 documents.
To disprove the said allegations, respondent-wife has examined herself as RW.1, her maternal uncle as RW.2 and her father as RW.3.

10. On consideration of entire evidence, both oral and documentary, vide impugned order dated 04.06.2012, learned Family Court granted decree of divorce dissolving the marriage of the appellant with respondent dated 24.06.1999.

However, learned Family Court has granted an amount of Rs.
5,00,000/- to the respondent and her son towards permanent alimony to be paid by the appellant within two months.
Feeling aggrieved by the KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 said order, the appellant-husband and respondent-wife preferred the present appeals.

sentences.text: On analysis of the entire evidence, both oral and documentary, learned Family Court held that respondent subjected the appellant to cruelty and she has deserted him.

In paragraph No.30,
learned Family Court gave a finding that respondent failed to prove that she attempted to commit suicide.

Learned Family Court after considering the deposition of RW.1 and admissions made by her during cross examination held that the contention of appellant-husband that the respondent is trying to project mental condition which is nothing but causing mental cruelty on the appellant cannot be ignored.
Learned Family Court also discussed about the mediations held by PW.2 to PW.4.
But respondent voluntarily deserted the appellant without any reasonable cause.
12. As per Exs.P5 to P13, the sale deed execution by the respondent, she has received more than 50,00,000/- as sale consideration, showing that her financial condition is better than the appellant.

Respondent has categorically admitted that Exs.P5 and P12 are the Sale Deeds executed by her in respect of Plot KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 Nos. 202 and 301 and Exs.P6, P8, P9 and P10 are the sale deeds executed by developers in respect of the flats fallen to their share

and the said documents would reveal the financial condition of the respondent.
13.
Learned Family Court also discussed about purchase of plot at Nizampet, respondent entering into a development agreement and appellant filing the aforesaid suit in paragraph No.32.
On the analysis of evidence, learned Family Court gave a specific finding that the respondent subjected the appellant to mental cruelty and she has deserted him.

14. As discussed supra, though the appellant and respondent are living separately since 2006,
appellant herein has filed aforesaid O.P. in the year 2009.
There is no possibility of reunion despite efforts made by PW2 to PW4.
There is no change in the attitude of respondent.
15. On consideration of the entire evidence, learned Family Court gave a specific finding that appellant was subjected to cruelty by respondent and deserted him.

Considering the fact that appellant is working as Cane Regulation Inspector under the Government of Andhra Pradesh, his admission that he is not KL,J & PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 looking after the welfare and education of the child since 2006, learned Family Court awarded an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- to the respondent and her son towards permanent alimony.
Therefore, the said order is a reasoned order and well founded.
It does not deserve any interference by this Court in the present appeals.

16. It is also relevant to note that even according to the respondent, during pendency of the present appeals despite the order of this Court dated 09.08.2012, appellant-husband remarried and he is living with second wife.
Even according to her, appellant is suffering with night blindness.
It is also relevant to note that the appellant herein is aged about 55 years and respondent is aged about 47 years.
Her son is aged about 25 years, he became major.

17. Learned counsel for respondent placed reliance on the principle laid down in S. Brahmanandam v. S. Rama Devi1, V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat2, Debananda Tamuli v. Smti Kakumoni Kataky3, Savitri Pandey v. Prem Chandra Pandey4, Samar 2017 (1) ALD 241 (DB) 1994 SCC (1) 337 2022 (3) ALD 5 S. Srinivas Reddy vs S. Neha and another 6, to contend that learned Family Court has failed to consider the fact that the allegation made by appellant husband against respondent wife do not constitute cruelty.

sentences.text: Cruelty is not defined in any statute.
Learned Family Court and this Court has to consider the allegations made by the appellant and come to a conclusion as to whether the said allegations constitute cruelty.

Learned Family Court cannot award an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- towards permanent alimony to his wife and son without calling for their assets and liabilities as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajnesh v. Neha (supra 6).

18. As discussed supra, learned Family Court, on considering the entire evidence both oral and documentary, gave a specific finding that the allegations made by appellant against respondent amounts to cruelty and the respondent subjected appellant to cruelty.

Considering the fact that appellant is working as Cane Regulating Inspector, learned Family Court has awarded said amount of Rs.5,00,000/- to the respondent and her son towards (2007) 4 SCC 511 (2021) 2 SCC 324 KL,J &
PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 permanent alimony.
Therefore, the impugned order is a reasoned order.

19. It is also not in dispute that at the instance of respondent wife, Police Yacharam have registered a case vide crime No.92 of 2001 against the appellant-husband and Smt Tippireddi Swapna D/o.
Tippireddi Janga Reddy and others for the offences under Section 498A, 506 and 494 of IPC.
On conclusion of investigation, the Investigation Officer laid charge sheet against them.
The said CC is pending.
According to the Investigating Officer, the said swapna is second wife of the appellant.

Thus, there are strained relations between the husband and wife.
20.

During the pendency of the aforesaid appeals, respondent- wife filed I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 to receive certain documents including medical reports dated 15.03.2007,
19.04.2005, 03.05.2005 etc.
According to her, she could not file the same before the trial Court since the same were not traced out.
She was under the impression that trial Court would believe her version.
Therefore, she filed the said IA to receive the said documents.

In paragraph No.4 of the affidavit filed in support of the said I.A., she has alleged that appellant-husband married for KL,J &
PSS,J F.C.A.Nos.229 and 297 of 2012 And I.A.No.1 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 second time in flagrant violation of the orders passed by this Court directing him not to remarry during the pendency of the appeals.
21. It is relevant to note that appellant-husband has filed aforesaid OP in February 2009, she has filed counter in the said OP in November 2009.
On consideration of the same, learned Family Court passed impugned order dated 04.06.2012.
Respondent preferred an appeal vide F.C.A.No.229 of 2012 on 01.08.2012.
Even then she has filed the present application only on 12.02.2024.
She has not explained about the said abnormal delay in filing the documents.
The only explanation offered by her that the said documents were not traced is not convincing.
It is a vague contention.

Therefore,
the said IA is liable to be dismissed and accordingly dismissed.
